structured_output.what_is_happening: A Solana token "Split"/$SPLIT (contract DxAZrr...SxZ) migrated from a pump.fun-style curve to a PumpSwap pool roughly 10-16 minutes before the detection trigger, pumping +156-164% in its first hour on ~$198k volume against a ~$108-111k market cap (h1 turnover ~7.2x). It is one of at least ten near-identical "SPLIT"/"Split" tokens created within the same ~16-minute window, ranging from $5k to $404k market cap; a sibling contract (DRKGY...pump) is ~4x larger with ~$1.08M h1 volume, suggesting either a coordinated multi-deploy by the same team/brand or a snipe-war on a trending name. The associated project, UseSplit (usesplit.pro / @Use_Split), is a real, live Solana product ("split token fees through X Money") with a working site, docs, and a "$SPLIT Buybacks" nav item, but no contract address or tokenomics are posted on the landing page, and I could not confirm organic X/Twitter discussion of the ticker or contract (search engines index X poorly; the handle was not directly surfaced via site:x.com search). GMGN data shows zero smart-money/KOL wallets, no paid DexScreener promotion, but 74 bundler wallets and one single non-pool wallet holding 80.05% of circulating supply (top10 = 85.24%). RugCheck flags "Large Amount of LP Unlocked (99.99%)" as danger-level on one of two markets (lp_locked_pct_top_markets = [0%, 79.25%]), even though the packet's own rug-guard filter classified this specific pair as non-removable (LP burned) and let it through — a real tension in the data. Price had already pulled back -12.47% in the 5 minutes before detection, right after the +156% hourly spike, i.e. entry happens shortly after a large move that may already be topping.

narrative.description: UseSplit is a Solana payments/fee-splitting product with a live but preview-status website and a token buyback mechanic referenced in its nav. This is a real, if niche, product-driven narrative rather than a viral meme or news event.
narrative.why_spreading: No external cultural/news catalyst found for the 'Split' name. The apparent 'spread' is really a swarm of ~10 near-identical same-name token launches within 16 minutes, which looks more like a serial-relaunch or ticker-farming pattern (creator's X account has launched 20 tokens per GMGN) than organic multi-community narrative spread. Volume/turnover is real but concentrated in a very short window typical of pump.fun-migration mechanics, not evidence of the underlying product idea catching on.

token_connection.why_this_token: This is one of at least 10 same-name 'SPLIT' pairs launched within the same ~16-minute window; it is not the largest by market cap or volume (a sibling pair has ~4x the market cap and ~5x the h1 volume), so it is unclear this is the one traders/searchers converge on.
token_connection.competing_tokens: At least 9 other SPLIT/Split contracts in the packet, market caps $5k-$404k; largest sibling (DRKGY...pump) has $404k mcap and $1.08M h1 volume vs this token's $108-111k mcap and $198k h1 volume.

authenticity.evidence: No paid DexScreener promotion flags are set (dexscreener_paid_ad/boost/trending all false), no smart-money or renowned wallets, no degen-call count, and buys-per-unique-buyer ratio (~1.58) is close to organic. 634 unique buyers vs 106 unique sellers in the first hour is a genuinely broad participant count for a ~15-minute-old pool.
authenticity.uncertainty: Could not verify any actual X/Twitter posts, Telegram, Discord, Reddit or news discussion in the 4-search budget available — X is poorly indexed by search engines and the @Use_Split handle itself did not surface via site:x.com. 74 bundler wallets and one wallet holding 80% of circulating supply raise real doubt about how organic the buyer count is versus wash/bundle-assisted volume feeding into that buyer count.

structural_risks: Single non-pool wallet holds 80.05% of circulating supply; top10 holders = 85.24% — a dump from this wallet would crater price independent of LP status
74 bundler wallets and 64 'top' wallets among ~661 holders, consistent with coordinated early accumulation
RugCheck flags 'Large Amount of LP Unlocked' as danger-level on one of two markets, in tension with the packet's own rug-guard classification of this pair as non-removable
Only $27-28k total liquidity against a $108-111k market cap — thin depth for a token that already moved +156% in an hour
Token is one of ~10 same-name clones, diluting and fragmenting any attention/liquidity that does exist
Price already pulled back -12.47% in the 5 minutes before entry, suggesting the initial spike may be exhausting right as the trade begins

structured_output.counterargument: My read leans bearish on concentration and clone-swarm dynamics, but the raw flow data (1011 buys vs 563 sells h1, 634 unique buyers, h1 turnover 7.2x, mint/freeze renounced, LP burned per rug_guard, zero honeypot/tax flags) is genuinely strong for a sub-$300k, ~15-minute-old pool, and this is exactly the kind of high-velocity early pump.fun graduate that the prereg's base rate (1-in-8 hits +100% before -50% within 6h in the looser prior version) was built to catch — an even-earlier, smaller-cap version could plausibly have fatter tails in both directions. The 80% single holder could simply be a bonding-curve-era early buyer with no urgent reason to sell in the next 30 minutes, and the -12% five-minute dip could be routine post-spike consolidation before a second leg rather than a top.

structured_output.thesis: This is a fast, high-turnover pump.fun graduate riding a genuinely broad buyer count (634 unique buyers in ~15 minutes), but it sits inside a swarm of ~10 same-named token clones (with a larger, higher-volume sibling competing for the same attention), carries an 80%-single-wallet supply overhang, and shows a -12% pullback right at the moment of entry — a profile that looks more like a serial-relaunch ticker farm catching bots and bundlers than an organically spreading narrative. I rank it below a typical coin in this pool: the raw flow numbers are respectable, but concentration risk and clone-swarm attention fragmentation are exactly the kind of structural red flags that separate short-lived spikes from real runners.
